name: Kapardeeswarar Temple, Tiruvalanchuzhi
deity: Shiva as Kapardeeswarar (Karpaganathar), with the goddess Periyanayaki
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine near Swamimalai, sung in the Tevaram (7th century), with Chola and Nayak work
summary: At Tiruvalanchuzhi near Swamimalai, Shiva is Kapardeeswarar, but the temple is loved above all for Swetha Vinayakar, a white Ganesha said to have been fashioned of sea-foam at the churning of the ocean.

sections.history: Tiruvalanchuzhi is an old Shaiva village in the Kaveri delta near Swamimalai, and its temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam praised by Appar and Thirugnana Sambandar. The Lord is worshipped as Kapardeeswarar, also called Karpaganathar, and the goddess as Periyanayaki. The oldest stonework belongs to the Chola period, and the Thanjavur Nayaks of the sixteenth century added substantially to the complex, as inscriptions of Chola and Nayak donations record. The village name, read as the place where the river turned, is linked in tradition to the winding course of the Kaveri drawn here by sages and gods.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian manner with a gopuram gateway, pillared halls and a temple tank. The sanctum holds the Shiva linga of Kapardeeswarar, with Periyanayaki in her shrine. Its most celebrated feature is the shrine of Swetha Vinayakar, the white Ganesha, worshipped with offerings made not to the fragile image directly but to a silver and gold frame before it. Carved mandapams and the delta's characteristic brick-and-stucco towers complete the temple.
sections.legends: When the gods and asuras churned the ocean of milk for the nectar of immortality, they are said to have begun without first worshipping Ganesha, and obstacles arose. To set this right a Ganesha was fashioned from the pure white foam of the ocean, and that Swetha Vinayakar came to be enshrined at Tiruvalanchuzhi. Because the image is of sea-foam and must not be bathed, worship is offered to the frame before it. The temple also keeps the tradition of the Kaveri's winding course being settled here.
sections.festivals: Vinayaka Chaturthi is observed with special grandeur, given the fame of Swetha Vinayakar, alongside Maha Shivaratri, the monthly Pradosham, and the Tamil month festivals. The car festival draws devotees from the surrounding delta towns. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally.
sections.experience: Most who come to Tiruvalanchuzhi make straight for the white Ganesha, one of the loved Ganesha shrines of the delta, before worshipping Kapardeeswarar and Periyanayaki in the main sanctums. Close to Kumbakonam and Swamimalai, the temple is an easy addition to a day of delta temple visits, and keeps the quiet dignity of an old village sanctuary.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvalanchuzhi lies about 6 km from Kumbakonam and close to Swamimalai in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest railway station and Tiruchirappalli the nearest airport (about 90 km). Local buses and autos serve the village.
